body:
## What it is

WeGoTrip sells this as a self-guided tour in Rome, Italy. The listing gives its length as 1.5 hours, over a route of about 3.1 km. It starts at Santa Maria in Trastevere, Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere. The tour plays in the WeGoTrip app on your own phone. WeGoTrip names Leonardo as the tour's author.

## How WeGoTrip describes it

> Rebel Rome is a self-guided audio walk through Trastevere and up the Janiculum, where the voices of the streets meet the story of a city that challenged papal power. Start whenever you like at Santa Maria in Trastevere, with the audio playing on your own phone. Around you, glasses clink and conversation fills the square. This is the Rome Giuseppe Gioachino Belli brought into his 2279 sonnets, writing in Romanesco, the language people spoke in the streets.
>
> Above the neighbourhood, you find another side of that independent spirit. Rome had been a republic for barely three months when France sent an army to restore the pope to power. From the Janiculum, you look across the rooftops and domes with that struggle in mind. Down in Trastevere, the Carmelite convent beside Santa Maria della Scala became a hospital during the fighting: a place where the city made room for its wounded.
>
> Between the busy squares and the quieter climb, you hear how poetry and resistance belong to the same streets. The walk ends beside the Tiber at Ponte Sisto, with the voices of Trastevere still around you.
